requirements.title: Statement entities include implied-DO variables, statement-function dummies, and FORALL statement indices, and shadow other identifiers in their statement scope
requirements.definition: A data-i-do-variable, ac-do-variable, statement-function dummy, or FORALL statement index is a statement entity. A same-spelling statement entity is interpreted as the statement entity within its scope even though another identifier with that spelling is in scope.

pending.statement-entity-class-list: Source-use plan links DATA implied DO, array constructor implied DO, statement functions, and FORALL statement catalogues to their statement-entity role without duplicating syntax rules.
pending.statement-entity-shadows-outer-identifie: Runtime plan includes both array-constructor and DATA implied-DO sentinels. Array constructor: outer INTEGER :: i is set to 99, evaluate a=[(i, i=1,3)], expect a=[1,2,3] and outer i still 99 after the statement. DATA: declare INTEGER :: i = 99 and INTEGER :: a(3); DATA (a(i), i = 1, 3) / 10, 20, 30 / initializes a before execution, so execution only observes a == [10,20,30] and i == 99; the DATA implied-DO i is the statement entity, not the initialized outer i.

requirements.title: DATA and array-constructor implied-DO variables have implied-DO scope, integer scalar type, no other attributes, and no containing-scope declaration effect
requirements.definition: The data-i-do-variable or ac-do-variable has the scope of its implied DO, is a scalar variable, has the explicit integer type-spec type and parameters or those supplied by the enclosing implicit rules, must be integer, has no other attributes, and does not implicitly declare a containing-scope variable.

pending.implied-do-variable-scope-only-implied-d: Runtime plan uses outer INTEGER :: i=99 with a=[(i, i=1,3)] expecting a=[1,2,3] and i still 99, plus DATA (a(i), i=1,3) /10,20,30/ with i initialized in its declaration, expecting a=[10,20,30] and i still 99 after execution observes the DATA-initialized objects.
pending.implied-do-variable-scalar: Source-use plan keeps the ac-do-variable as a scalar name and delegates non-scalar designator rejection to array-constructor/DO-variable syntax owners.
pending.inline-integer-type-spec-controls-type: Capability-selected runtime plan defines module kinds_mod with INTEGER, PARAMETER :: k2=SELECTED_INT_KIND(18); 7.4.3.1 p2 guarantees that integer kind exists, so INTEGER(k2) is conforming. The discriminating row is selected only with k2 /= KIND(0), matching tests/profiles/two_integer_kinds.f90, which probes count(integer_kinds /= kind(0)) > 0; processors with k2 == KIND(0) skip this row as non-discriminating. The explicit ac-implied-do [(KIND(j), INTEGER(k2) :: j = 1, 1)] yields [k2]. An outer default INTEGER :: j = 99 remains outside the implied-DO scope with KIND(j)==KIND(0) and value 99.
pending.implicit-rules-control-implied-do-type: Capability-selected runtime plan defines module kinds_mod with INTEGER, PARAMETER :: k2=SELECTED_INT_KIND(18); 7.4.3.1 p2 guarantees that integer kind exists, so IMPLICIT INTEGER(KIND=k2) is conforming. The test scoping unit has USE kinds_mod, ONLY: k2 before IMPLICIT, then IMPLICIT INTEGER(KIND=k2) (i). The discriminating row is selected only with k2 /= KIND(0), matching tests/profiles/two_integer_kinds.f90, which probes count(integer_kinds /= kind(0)) > 0; processors with k2 == KIND(0) skip this row as non-discriminating. The selected row evaluates [(KIND(i), i=1,1)] expecting [k2], proving the ac-do-variable kind comes from enclosing implicit rules rather than default integer.
pending.implied-do-variable-must-be-integer: Source-control plan names existing owner doc/catalogues/implicit_statement_8_7.json: under IMPLICIT REAL (r) attempt [(r, r=1,3)] and use a control changing only the implicit letter rule to INTEGER; no mandatory diagnostic is claimed for this unnumbered restriction.
pending.implied-do-variable-no-other-attributes: Source-use plan confirms no POINTER, TARGET, SAVE, or host attributes are inferred from an outer homonym; observable value plan keeps only scalar integer behavior.
pending.implied-do-variable-not-host-declaration: Runtime plan declares outer INTEGER :: i=99 before [(i,i=1,3)] and asserts i remains 99. Companion DATA plan declares INTEGER :: i = 99 and INTEGER :: a(3); DATA (a(i), i=1,3) /10,20,30/ initializes a before execution, and execution observes a=[10,20,30] and i=99, showing the DATA implied-DO variable did not become the containing-scope variable.

requirements.title: Statement-function dummy arguments have statement scope, scalar type from enclosing rules, and no other attributes
